cases.why_in_scope: The skill requires one logical change per commit ("if it needs 'and', split it") and messages in the form type(scope): subject with an imperative subject, no trailing period, and a body explaining what and why wrapped at 72 characters. Here the staged set holds four unrelated changes (a bug fix, a pure rename, a dependency bump and docs), so the skill pushes the model to recommend splitting them into separate typed commits. A strong model without the skill may simply write one nicer combined message as asked, or use the team's past-tense style ("Исправил…", "обновил…").
rubric: Recommends splitting the staged changes into separate commits (the timezone fix, the rename, the requests bump and the README change as distinct commits) rather than one combined commit, with a brief reason (e.g. easier revert, review or bisect); offering a single-commit fallback is fine as long as splitting is the recommendation.
Proposed commit subjects use the type(scope): subject form with fitting types: fix for the timezone bug, refactor for the renames, chore (or build) for the requests bump, docs for the README.
Subjects are imperative (e.g. "fix"/"add", or Russian infinitive/imperative such as "исправить", not past tense like "исправил"/"added") and have no trailing period.

The fix commit body states what was wrong and why (invoice date computed in UTC instead of the client's timezone, so Vladivostok clients got the previous day) and references BILL-412; the answer does not describe the rename as a behaviour change.

history.content: Can you write a commit message for my changes? I swapped the O(n^2) duplicate check in `src/search/dedupe.ts` for a Set-based one (p95 on /search went from 840ms to 95ms on our 20k-item fixture). While I was in there I also ran prettier over the whole `src/search/` folder since the formatting was a mess, 14 files touched in total.

Sure, here's a message you can use:

```
perf(search): Replaced quadratic dedupe with Set-based lookup.

The duplicate check in dedupe.ts compared every result against every other result, which was O(n^2) and dominated /search latency on large result sets. It now tracks seen ids in a Set, bringing p95 on the 20k-item fixture from 840ms to 95ms. Also ran prettier across src/search/ to fix inconsistent formatting.
```
